title: Provision an attested proxy → native principal association so the agent facade can resolve a remote root's proxy id
outcome: Provision an attested proxy → native principal association so the agent facade can resolve a remote root's proxy id
acceptance: A production provisioning or refresh operation establishes a host-local association from a specific local UI proxy record to an eligible native root session's current central mailbox principal. Evidence comes through the authenticated enrolled-host/central-placement path and binds the proxy/configuration identity, native host/session/creation identity, central authority epoch, enrollment/configuration freshness and placement generation. Matching names, endpoint text, raw session ids or RemoteConfig.id strings alone cannot establish it. The proxy remains a proxy and gains neither native participant binding nor sender authority; unrelated standalone sessions are not adopted.

Through the ordinary termal_send_to_session facade, a valid associated local proxy handle resolves to the same current canonical participant and central mailbox as the directory's domain-session id, with the ordinary API receiving that canonical id. The federated HTTP API continues to reject unresolved raw proxy/native ids; standalone API behavior and central ACL/self/root-session checks remain intact. Success creates no second participant or mailbox, and assignment/report/reply authority continues to flow through C.

Missing, ambiguous, stale or conflicting association, revoked enrollment, changed authority/placement/configuration identity, removed/recreated proxy or native session, and collisions of raw session ids across hosts cannot resolve to the wrong participant or silently retarget a stale reference. Central unavailability fails visibly without local mailbox fallback or treating cached association as current authority. After restart/reconnect, the association is used only after current validation or explicit authenticated re-establishment; an old idempotent intent is never rewritten to a successor principal.

Deterministic tests establish the association through production provisioning/refresh behavior, then invoke the actual MCP facade and ordinary HTTP path. They cover canonical/proxy equivalence, raw-proxy HTTP refusal, absence of the association, cross-host raw-id collisions, recreation/stale authority and central outage/recovery. Fixture-only string equality or injected fake native bindings are not positive evidence. M5's final one-C/two-S integration includes the associated-proxy tool path while preserving the required canonical path and reports deferred or simulated coverage honestly.

Exact-input focused tests and the full five-stage gate pass, and the independent read-only review pair has no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding. Evidence records the accepted dependency revisions and the actual identity/provisioning path used; loopback evidence is not reported as live Mac/O1 readiness.
